Researchers compared catalase activity in three enzyme samples prepared at different pH values and hydrogen peroxide concentrations. Each sample was mixed with hydrogen peroxide, and the volume of oxygen produced was recorded at several times. Table 1 identifies the preparation conditions for samples A–C, while Figure 1 shows the oxygen volume measured for each sample over time. The same sample labels are used in both displays.

According to Table 1 and Figure 1, what oxygen volume was produced by the sample prepared at pH 7 after 6 min?
items.explanation: Table 1 identifies Sample B as the sample prepared at pH 7. At 6 min, the Sample B line in Figure 1 is at 38 mL.

per_choice.correct: Table 1 identifies Sample B as the sample prepared at pH 7. At 6 min, the Sample B line in Figure 1 is at 38 mL.
per_choice.trap: The choices 17 mL and 21 mL come from Sample C at 6 min and Sample A at 8 min; 48 mL is Sample B at 8 min rather than 6 min.

items.trap: The choices 17 mL and 21 mL come from Sample C at 6 min and Sample A at 8 min; 48 mL is Sample B at 8 min rather than 6 min.

Table 1 gives the initial oxygen-production rate and the total oxygen produced after 20 minutes for each temperature. Figure 1 tracks cumulative oxygen production over 20 minutes at three of the temperatures. For this experiment, the slope of a line in Figure 1 represents the oxygen-production rate, and a constant slope would predict cumulative oxygen equal to rate multiplied by time.

If the rates remain constant beyond 20 minutes, what does combining Table 1 with Figure 1 imply about oxygen production at 40 C compared with 30 C after an additional 10 minutes?
choices: The 40 C sample will remain below the 30 C sample, and the difference in cumulative oxygen will increase.
The 40 C sample will remain below the 30 C sample, but the difference in cumulative oxygen will remain fixed.
The 40 C sample will catch up to the 30 C sample because both lines begin at zero.
The 40 C sample will exceed the 30 C sample because its 20-minute value is closer to the 30 C value than its initial rate is.
items.explanation: Figure 1 shows the 40 C line has a smaller slope than the 30 C line, consistent with Table 1 rates of 2.0 and 3.1 mL O2/min. Thus, the 30 C sample gains about 1.1 mL more each minute, so the gap widens during the next 10 minutes.

per_choice.correct: Figure 1 shows the 40 C line has a smaller slope than the 30 C line, consistent with Table 1 rates of 2.0 and 3.1 mL O2/min. Thus, the 30 C sample gains about 1.1 mL more each minute, so the gap widens during the next 10 minutes.
per_choice.trap: The second choice treats a difference between endpoints as if it were fixed despite unequal slopes; the other choices reverse the line trend or compare the wrong measurements.

items.trap: The second choice treats a difference between endpoints as if it were fixed despite unequal slopes; the other choices reverse the line trend or compare the wrong measurements.

Which conclusion about the constant-rate model is supported by all of Table 1 and Figure 1 without extending the conclusion beyond the tested conditions?

items.stem:
Researchers tested whether salt stress reduces seedling performance because of reduced water potential, sodium-specific toxicity, or both. Radish seeds were grown for 8 days in nutrient solution containing either sodium chloride (NaCl) or polyethylene glycol (PEG), a compound that lowers water potential but is not taken up by roots. A later calibration showed that 50 mM NaCl and 100 g/L PEG produced approximately the same water potential, while 100 mM NaCl and 200 g/L PEG were also matched; researchers additionally found that a sodium transporter becomes active above 75 mM NaCl. Table 1 reports germination and root length, and Figure 1 tracks root growth for the two higher-concentration treatments.

Which comparison from Table 1 most directly separates an effect caused by reduced water potential from an additional effect caused by sodium ions?
choices: The control and the 50 mM NaCl treatment
The 100 mM NaCl and 200 g/L PEG treatments
The 100 mM NaCl and 100 g/L PEG treatments
The 50 mM NaCl and 200 g/L PEG treatments
items.explanation: The 100 mM NaCl and 200 g/L PEG treatments have the same water potential, so differences between them are not explained by water potential alone.

per_choice.correct: The 100 mM NaCl and 200 g/L PEG treatments have the same water potential, so differences between them are not explained by water potential alone.
per_choice.trap: The other comparisons either use unequal water potentials or compare NaCl and PEG concentrations that were not calibrated as equivalent.

items.trap: The other comparisons either use unequal water potentials or compare NaCl and PEG concentrations that were not calibrated as equivalent.

choices: At matched water potentials, PEG consistently inhibits germination and root growth more than NaCl.
At the higher matched water potential stress, NaCl produces an additional inhibition beyond the effect of reduced water potential.
Root growth is unaffected by the type of solute because both treatments eventually produce roots.
The lower-concentration treatments show that water potential has no relationship to germination.
items.explanation: At the matched −0.42 MPa condition, the NaCl treatment has lower germination and shorter roots in Table 1, and its root-growth curve remains below the PEG curve in Figure 1.

per_choice.correct: At the matched −0.42 MPa condition, the NaCl treatment has lower germination and shorter roots in Table 1, and its root-growth curve remains below the PEG curve in Figure 1.

A later calibration showed that 50 mM NaCl and 100 g/L PEG produced approximately the same water potential, while 100 mM NaCl and 200 g/L PEG were also matched; researchers additionally found that a sodium transporter becomes active above 75 mM NaCl. Table 1 reports germination and root length, and Figure 1 tracks root growth for the two higher-concentration treatments.

If the sodium transporter were completely blocked in the 100 mM NaCl treatment, which outcome would best fit the information in the passage and the displays?
choices: Germination and final root length would likely approach the values for 200 g/L PEG rather than the control values.
Germination would likely rise to about 92%, and final root length would likely rise to about 38 mm.
Germination and final root length would likely remain near 61% and 20 mm because water potential would be unchanged.
Germination and final root length would likely fall below the current NaCl values because blocking transport increases osmotic stress.
items.explanation: The transporter is a proposed route for sodium-specific toxicity. Blocking it should remove much of the difference between the matched NaCl and PEG treatments, while the unchanged water potential would still impose stress; the PEG values are therefore the appropriate comparison.

per_choice.correct: The transporter is a proposed route for sodium-specific toxicity. Blocking it should remove much of the difference between the matched NaCl and PEG treatments, while the unchanged water potential would still impose stress; the PEG values are therefore the appropriate comparison.
per_choice.trap: The second choice assumes removal of sodium toxicity removes all water-potential stress, while the third and fourth ignore the stated role and direction of sodium uptake.

The researchers plan to test whether sodium-specific toxicity becomes stronger once the transporter is active. Which design would provide the most informative new comparison?
choices: Compare 150 mM NaCl with the control, without measuring water potential.
Compare 150 mM NaCl with 100 mM NaCl, using the same PEG concentration for both.
Compare 150 mM NaCl with a PEG solution calibrated to the same water potential, measuring both germination and root length over time.
Compare 200 g/L PEG with 100 g/L PEG, because both treatments avoid sodium uptake.
items.explanation: A PEG treatment matched to the 150 mM NaCl water potential controls for osmotic stress, while measurements of both endpoints and their time courses can reveal an additional sodium effect above the 75 mM transporter threshold.

per_choice.correct: A PEG treatment matched to the 150 mM NaCl water potential controls for osmotic stress, while measurements of both endpoints and their time courses can reveal an additional sodium effect above the 75 mM transporter threshold.
per_choice.trap: The other designs confound sodium effects with unequal water potential, use an uncontrolled PEG concentration, or test PEG alone without the needed NaCl comparison.

Researchers measured net dissolved-oxygen production by aquatic plants exposed to four colored light filters. Each filter was tested at a different irradiance and had a characteristic peak wavelength, as listed in Table 1. Figure 1 shows the cumulative net oxygen production measured over time for each filter. The researchers expected irradiance to influence oxygen production, but wavelength also differed among the filters.

The irradiance of which filter in Table 1 is 25 W/m² lower than that of the Red filter? According to Figure 1, what net oxygen production did that filter have at 15 min?
items.explanation: The Red filter had an irradiance of 120 W/m²; 25 W/m² lower is 95 W/m², which identifies the Blue filter in Table 1. The Blue series is at 6.9 mg/L at 15 min in Figure 1.

per_choice.correct: The Red filter had an irradiance of 120 W/m²; 25 W/m² lower is 95 W/m², which identifies the Blue filter in Table 1. The Blue series is at 6.9 mg/L at 15 min in Figure 1.
per_choice.trap: A reader may choose the Green row because it is lower than Red, or read the Blue value at 10 min instead of 15 min.

items.trap: A reader may choose the Green row because it is lower than Red, or read the Blue value at 10 min instead of 15 min.

Researchers placed aquatic plants under low, medium, or high light and measured nitrate concentration in the surrounding water every 2 hours for 10 hours. Dissolved oxygen was measured at the same times as an indicator of photosynthetic activity. The researchers expected intervals with increasing dissolved oxygen to show decreasing nitrate concentration if plant uptake was driven by photosynthesis. Figure 1 shows nitrate concentration, and Table 1 shows dissolved oxygen for each light condition.

According to Figure 1 and Table 1, during which interval did nitrate concentration decrease while dissolved oxygen also decreased?
items.explanation: Under high light from 6 to 8 h, nitrate decreased from 20 to 19 mg/L while oxygen decreased from 7.2 to 7.1 mg/L. The other listed intervals do not show both quantities decreasing.

per_choice.correct: Under high light from 6 to 8 h, nitrate decreased from 20 to 19 mg/L while oxygen decreased from 7.2 to 7.1 mg/L. The other listed intervals do not show both quantities decreasing.
per_choice.trap: A student may select the medium-light interval because its nitrate curve turns upward there, or select the high-light 8–10 h interval by overlooking that oxygen rises.

items.trap: A student may select the medium-light interval because its nitrate curve turns upward there, or select the high-light 8–10 h interval by overlooking that oxygen rises.

items.stem:
Researchers measured net oxygen production by an aquatic plant at several light intensities and nutrient levels. Figure 1 reports rates measured at 20°C, while Table 1 gives a temperature correction factor relative to the rate at 20°C. For temperatures between those listed in Table 1, the factor may be estimated by linear interpolation, and adjusted rate equals the Figure 1 rate multiplied by that factor. For light intensities above 300 μmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹, estimates may be made by extending the final segment of the appropriate Figure 1 series.

According to Table 1 and Figure 1, what is the estimated adjusted oxygen-production rate for the high-nutrient plant at a light intensity of 150 μmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ and a temperature of 25°C?
items.explanation: At 150, the high-nutrient rate is halfway between 5 and 9, or 7 mg/L/h. At 25°C, the factor is halfway between 1.00 and 1.15, or 1.075; 7 × 1.075 ≈ 7.5 mg/L/h.

per_choice.correct: At 150, the high-nutrient rate is halfway between 5 and 9, or 7 mg/L/h. At 25°C, the factor is halfway between 1.00 and 1.15, or 1.075; 7 × 1.075 ≈ 7.5 mg/L/h.
per_choice.trap: 5.9 uses the low-nutrient series; 7.0 ignores the temperature correction; 8.1 uses the 30°C correction factor instead of interpolating for 25°C.

items.trap: 5.9 uses the low-nutrient series; 7.0 ignores the temperature correction; 8.1 uses the 30°C correction factor instead of interpolating for 25°C.

Researchers monitored glucose consumption by yeast cultures maintained at 30°C. Figure 1 shows the glucose concentration remaining in each of two cultures at several times during fermentation. Figure 2 is a calibration plot relating glucose concentration to carbon dioxide production rate under the same assay conditions. A glucose concentration read from Figure 1 can therefore be used with Figure 2 to estimate the corresponding carbon dioxide production rate.

According to Figure 1 and Figure 2, how much lower is the estimated CO2 production rate for Trial 1 at 15 min than for Trial 1 at 10 min?
items.explanation: Figure 1 gives 8 g/L at 15 min and 12 g/L at 10 min for Trial 1. Figure 2 converts these to 24 mL/min and 31 mL/min, respectively, so the difference is 7 mL/min.

per_choice.correct: Figure 1 gives 8 g/L at 15 min and 12 g/L at 10 min for Trial 1. Figure 2 converts these to 24 mL/min and 31 mL/min, respectively, so the difference is 7 mL/min.
per_choice.trap: A student may use Trial 2's 15-min concentration or compare the glucose concentrations directly instead of converting both values through Figure 2.

items.trap: A student may use Trial 2's 15-min concentration or compare the glucose concentrations directly instead of converting both values through Figure 2.

A student recorded the mass of a dissolving tablet at several times after placing it in water. Table 1 lists the measured values, and Figure 1 plots the same measurements with straight line segments connecting successive points. The student used the plotted slope to compare how rapidly the tablet lost mass during different intervals. Because the measurements were not taken at equal time intervals, both the vertical change and the elapsed time must be considered.

Which statement correctly identifies a feature that must appear in both Table 1 and Figure 1?
choices: The mass is constant from 5 min to 7 min, so Figure 1 has a horizontal segment over that interval.
The mass is constant from 2 min to 5 min, so Figure 1 has a horizontal segment over that interval.
The mass decreases from 5 min to 7 min, so Figure 1 has its steepest negative segment over that interval.
The mass increases from 10 min to 12 min, so Figure 1 slopes upward over that interval.
items.explanation: Table 1 gives 13.8 g at both 5 and 7 min. Therefore, the corresponding segment in Figure 1 is horizontal.

Researchers investigated how pH affects the rate at which amylase hydrolyzes starch. Equal volumes of starch and amylase were mixed at pH 5, 7, or 9, and iodine absorbance was recorded at 2-minute intervals for 8 minutes; a no-enzyme mixture was measured in parallel. Because iodine absorbance increases with the amount of starch remaining, a calibration series was prepared before interpreting the reaction readings. The calibration data and reaction time-course data are shown below.

The pH 5, 7, and 9 mixtures have different absorbances at time 0 in Figure 1. Why was the time-0 reading necessary when comparing the mixtures?

It proves that the pH 9 mixture contained the most starch because its absorbance decreased the least
It supplies the zero-starch absorbance used in Table 1
It removes the need to use the no-enzyme mixture because all background effects occur at time 0

A researcher tested how the angle of a small solar panel and the incident irradiance affected its electrical current. For the angle trials, irradiance was held at 1,000 W/m^2; for the irradiance trials, the panel angle was held at 40 degrees. The researcher treated the angle effect between tested angles as approximately linear and treated current as approximately proportional to irradiance over the tested range. Table 1 and Figure 1 summarize the trials, including conditions that will be used to predict results for trials not run.

Using both Table 1 and Figure 1, which current would most reasonably be predicted for a trial at a panel angle of 50 degrees and an irradiance of 800 W/m^2?

Researchers grew identical algae cultures for 8 days while independently varying light intensity and nitrate concentration, measuring chlorophyll concentration as an indicator of algal growth. Table 1 gives the endpoint chlorophyll increase, and Figure 1 shows the increase over time for the same treatments. (1) Dr. Alvarez argued that nitrate is the primary limiting resource and predicted that increasing nitrate would produce a large growth increase even under reduced light. (2) Dr. Chen argued that light limits growth under shaded conditions and predicted that adding nitrate would have little effect when light is reduced, although nitrate should strongly affect cultures receiving full light.

Using both Table 1 and Figure 1, which comparison most directly supports Dr. Chen's claim that reduced light masks the effect of added nitrate?
choices: At day 8, adding nitrate increases chlorophyll by 16 µg/L at 100% light but only 6 µg/L at 40% light.
At day 8, reducing light decreases chlorophyll by 6 µg/L at low nitrate but by 16 µg/L at high nitrate.
At day 8, the high-nitrate culture under 40% light reaches 15 µg/L, which is higher than the low-nitrate culture under 40% light.
At day 2, the high-nitrate culture under 100% light reaches 5 µg/L, whereas the low-nitrate culture under 40% light reaches 2 µg/L.
items.explanation: The nitrate effect is 28 − 12 = 16 µg/L under full light but 15 − 9 = 6 µg/L under reduced light; Figure 1 shows the same separation developing over time.

per_choice.correct: The nitrate effect is 28 − 12 = 16 µg/L under full light but 15 − 9 = 6 µg/L under reduced light; Figure 1 shows the same separation developing over time.

Table 1 gives the initial oxygen-production rate, while Figure 1 shows cumulative oxygen production during the first 5 minutes. Before testing, the researchers expected activity to increase steadily as pH increased.

Which statement is consistent with both Table 1 and Figure 1?
choices: pH 8 produced the fastest initial reaction and the greatest cumulative oxygen volume after 5 minutes.
pH 10 produced the fastest initial reaction and the greatest cumulative oxygen volume after 5 minutes.
pH 6 produced more oxygen than pH 8 after 5 minutes, although its initial rate was lower.
pH 4 produced the fastest initial reaction, but pH 8 produced the greatest cumulative oxygen volume.

items.stem:
Researchers evaluated a model stating that yeast CO2 production increases with glucose concentration until the yeast enzymes become saturated; under those conditions, the rate should remain nearly constant unless ethanol inhibits the cells. Initial CO2-production rates were measured at 20°C and 30°C in cultures containing different glucose concentrations and no added ethanol. A second experiment followed cumulative CO2 production at 30°C in cultures containing 60 or 80 g/L glucose. Chemical analysis showed that glucose remained above 50 g/L in both cultures at 40 minutes, while the 80-g/L culture reached 15 g/L ethanol at 20 minutes; an independent assay showed that ethanol concentrations of at least 15 g/L reduce the production rate by half.

Which statement best reconciles the results in Table 1 and Figure 1 with the model and the added ethanol information?
choices: The 80-g/L culture had a lower initial rate than the 60-g/L culture, so its later lower CO2 production was expected from the beginning.
The 80-g/L culture produced more CO2 rapidly throughout the experiment because its glucose concentration was higher.
The similar initial rates at 30°C suggest enzyme saturation, whereas the later decline in the 80-g/L culture is consistent with ethanol inhibition.
The 60-g/L culture accumulated more ethanol by 20 minutes, causing its CO2 curve to become linear.
items.explanation: Table 1 shows nearly equal initial rates at 30°C for 60 and 80 g/L glucose, consistent with saturation. Figure 1 shows the 80-g/L culture slowing after 20 minutes, when the passage states that ethanol reached the inhibitory concentration.

per_choice.correct: Table 1 shows nearly equal initial rates at 30°C for 60 and 80 g/L glucose, consistent with saturation. Figure 1 shows the 80-g/L culture slowing after 20 minutes, when the passage states that ethanol reached the inhibitory concentration.
per_choice.trap: The tempting error is to use the higher glucose concentration to assume the 80-g/L curve remains higher, ignoring the later trend and the added ethanol fact.
